Keep its exact shape, colours and layout; it stands upright and never changes.
pouch_block: Each pouch is the real SoFyre pouch from the pouch reference photo: a plain WHITE soft non-woven sachet about the size of a palm, slightly puffy, rectangular, with zig-zag pinked sealed edges and no print. Not a tea bag, not a box, not a packet with writing.

shots.vo: This is going to matter once it gets cold outside.
shots.still: Close mid shot of a pantry shelf at eye level. The black SoFyre bag stands upright on the shelf filling the left two thirds of the frame, front facing the camera, its zip top open. Grace's hand enters from the right frame edge and pinches one white pouch by its top edge between thumb and index finger, lifting it out of the open bag.
shots.video: From the first frame the hand lifts the white pouch up out of the open bag and swings it toward the camera beside the bag; at the same time the camera pushes in and arcs a little to the left; the bag stays upright and unchanged with its front facing the camera the whole time.

shots.vo: Because guess who's looking for somewhere warm to live? Mice.
shots.still: Low camera at ground level by the closed white garage door of a house on a cold autumn evening, frost on the grass and leaves on the driveway; a small grey field mouse sits on the concrete near the narrow gap under the garage door.
shots.video: The small grey mouse scurries fast along the bottom of the garage door and squeezes under the gap into the garage; the low camera dollies quickly toward the door following it, fallen leaves skittering in the wind. One mouse only.

shots.vo: And you won't even know until there are droppings in your pantry.
shots.still: Close-up of the corner of a white pantry shelf: a handful of tiny dark mouse droppings scattered on the shelf next to the chewed bottom corner of a paper flour bag and a cereal box. Bright, clean, realistic, not gory.
shots.video: Handheld camera walks into the pantry and pushes in fast to the shelf corner, then eases to a stop on the droppings; nothing on the shelf moves.

shots.vo: So put these out now. Just drop one wherever they get in. The pantry,
shots.still: Pantry floor-level shelf corner behind canned food; Grace's hand enters from the right frame edge holding one white pouch pinched by its edge, about to set it down in the back corner.
shots.video: The camera moves forward with the hand as it reaches in and sets the white pouch down flat in the back corner behind the cans, lets go and pulls out of frame to the right; the camera keeps pushing in to the pouch.

shots.still: Open cabinet under a kitchen sink: white pipes, a few cleaning bottles with no labels, clean cabinet floor. Grace's hand enters from the bottom frame edge pinching one white pouch, placing it on the cabinet floor beside the pipe.
shots.video: The hand presses the white pouch down onto the cabinet floor beside the pipe, lets go and pulls back out of frame at the bottom edge; the camera tilts down slightly and eases back.

shots.still: Garage shelf at waist height near the side door, the parked silver car soft in the background. Grace's hand enters from the right frame edge setting one white pouch on the shelf.
shots.video: The hand sets the white pouch on the shelf and leaves frame; the camera trucks left along the shelf and swings around toward the parked silver car in one smooth move. The car does not move.

shots.vo: It's peppermint and cinnamon oil, so it smells fresh to us, but mice don't like it.
shots.still: Kitchen counter at a low three-quarter angle: the black SoFyre bag stands upright, front facing the camera; in front of it lie two white pouches, a fresh green mint sprig and three cinnamon sticks.
shots.video: Fast smooth orbit of the camera around the front of the bag from left to right with a slight rise, only the camera moves, the bag stays upright facing the camera, nothing on the counter moves.

shots.vo: No toxic chemicals, so it's safe around kids and pets.
shots.still: Hallway corner by the wall: one white pouch tucked on the floor behind the potted plant at the baseboard; a friendly golden retriever walks along the hallway toward the camera, past the plant.
shots.video: The golden retriever trots past the plant and the pouch toward the camera without touching the pouch while the low camera tracks backward ahead of it. One dog only.

shots.vo: And honestly, the best part? No traps to empty.
shots.still: An open kitchen drawer seen from above at an angle, neat utensils, one white pouch lying in the back corner of the drawer; Grace's hand at the front edge of the drawer, fingers curled around the drawer front.
shots.video: The hand pushes the drawer closed with its fingertips on the drawer front and lets go; the camera rises and pushes in over the closing drawer. The pouch inside stays plain white.

shots.vo: There are twelve in a bag and each one lasts up to three months,
shots.still: Bright kitchen counter, straight-on: the black SoFyre bag stands upright at the back, front facing the camera; in front of it exactly twelve white pouches lie flat in two neat rows of six.
shots.video: The camera starts low over the two rows of pouches and cranes up and forward to the bag front in one smooth move; nothing on the counter moves, the count of pouches never changes.

shots.vo: so grab two bags and do the whole house before the cold hits. It's in the orange cart.
shots.still: Kitchen island by a bright window with autumn trees outside: ONE black SoFyre bag stands upright, front facing the camera, a few white pouches lying beside it.
shots.video: Smooth arc-and-push dolly around the bag from the right until its front fills the frame, autumn leaves blowing past the window behind; the bag stays upright and unchanged. One bag only.
